Done. Here is what I built.

I wrote **STRATEGY.md** for Cognivo LMS (white-label instance `nigeria-demo`), the strategy-and-viability artifact for the plan stage: positioning (a brandable, deployable completion-to-credential platform, not another MOOC), the wedge (one organisation that wants its own branded instance, where the four-persona oversight model is the differentiator), and a current "why now" grounded in a fresh last-30-days read — most notably that the Coursera–Udemy merger has now **closed** (reported 11 May 2026, FTC early termination 9 Feb 2026), which hardens the PRD's "announced, status unknown" and confirms we should not fight for consumer learners. It also lays out the business model (revenue captured per-instance, not per-learner, so we avoid the traffic wall), carries forward the PRD's single riskiest assumption (does the demo convert to a funded deployment) with concrete consequences for the build, holds the confirmed scope line with deferred roadmap items listed explicitly, and sets build and business success metrics plus a per-instance north star (certificates issued per active cohort). I stayed in the CEO lane and did not write PLAN.md — that file-level build plan belongs to the eng specialist on this team.

Done. Report:

I wrote the engineering plan for Cognivo LMS as the eng teammate, staying in my lane (the CEO owns STRATEGY.md). **PLAN.md** is the file-level build plan: chosen stack (Node/TS + Express + raw-`pg` repository layer over Postgres, React/Vite + Recharts front end), the full data model (24 tables on an `org_id` tenancy spine), the complete REST surface, a named file tree with per-file responsibilities for both `server/` and `web/`, and a strict 6-phase sequence (skeleton/operability → identity → catalogue → the four flows → history/dashboards → a11y) with a verification gate on each phase. **ARCHITECTURE.md** records the load-bearing decisions — most importantly how the brief's "no-login persona switch" and the Forge Identity mandate coexist (persona buttons open *real* seeded sessions via a demo-only endpoint; RBAC and tenant isolation are enforced server-side in every profile) plus governance, residency, cookie-Secure-from-`x-forwarded-proto`, and the rules-default/optional-LLM roadmap. I also wrote the three plan-time declarations: **forge.dependencies.json** (postgres required; oidc/smtp/ai optional with clean degradation), **SCOPE.json** (17 features, each carrying "fits 375px" + "meets AA" in its definition of done, deferred items listed), and **forge.acceptance.json** (HTTP-probe criteria bound to features, with unauth-rejection checks and an auth block). One flag for the build stage: the acceptance `credentials.password` is a `SEED_PASSWORD` placeholder — the seed and the probe must be wired to the same injected value.

Done. I built the product & UX shape for Cognivo LMS (`nigeria-demo`, default brand "Nigeria Demo") as two artifacts:

**`DESIGN.md`** — the full design system and screen-by-screen UX spec: an AA-verified light+dark token set (every text/control/focus contrast ratio computed, not eyeballed — e.g. primary button unified to `#4f46e5` at 6.29:1, control borders ≥3:1, muted ink 4.98:1), the component library mapped 1:1 to `PLAN.md`'s `web/src/components/*`, every page's layout with its loading/empty/error states, the four core flows as journeys (including the completion-gated feedback thread and the "suggested path" roadmap framing), a dataviz spec using the validator-passed categorical palette with the light-mode relief rule (direct labels + table view) baked in, the white-label theming contract, and the yellow clam-shell spec.

**`wireframe.html`** — a self-contained, keyboard-operable prototype (working Light/Dark/System toggle, roving-tabindex screen switcher, skip link, semantic landmarks, labelled controls) rendering home/catalogue/course-feedback/learner/provider/owner screens with live inline charts; built to pass the Forge gate by construction — no fixed width >375px outside a media query (the one wide table sits in a `tabindex="0"` scroll container) and AA contrast in both themes.

Scope held to PRD §6; deferred items (cohorts/deadlines, proctoring, freemium, enterprise, feedback editing, degree tiers) are listed as acknowledged-but-not-designed-out, with the IA shaped to add them additively.

I wrote **DX.md**, the plan-stage developer-experience and maintainability contract for Cognivo LMS, layered over the existing PLAN/ARCHITECTURE/DESIGN/STRATEGY artifacts without duplicating them. It fixes a sub-5-minute, two-command Time-To-Hello-World (Docker demo profile), pins the exact root `npm` scripts contract so every workflow is one named command that can't drift, sets the boot-config and runtime error-message standards (problem→cause→fix, name the missing var, safe client envelope + request-id correlation, optional deps degrade with messages that mirror `forge.dependencies.json` verbatim), and lays out the maintainability rules that make instance N+1 configuration rather than a rewrite (strict typing, thin routes, `orgId`-first repositories, single sources for CSV/audit/theme, consistent naming, no dead code). It also specifies the required table-of-contents for the build's README.md and OPERATIONS.md, the contributor/CI workflow, a 9-point DX scorecard with how each item is proven, and the add-a-feature grain a new engineer follows.

The auth & session slice works end-to-end against the gate's declared probe (correct creds → 200 + `cognivo_session` cookie, `/api/auth/me` returns the owner, bad password → 401).

I test-drove it with three new cases in `test/api.test.js` (login success + cookie, bad-password 401, `/me` with/without session); all 17 tests pass. The no-login persona demo is untouched — this adds the credential path the acceptance contract requires without rebuilding anything.

report:
Verification complete. I booted the server fresh and probed every acceptance criterion against the live process rather than trusting the teammate reports — all pass end-to-end.

**Outcome (integration — no code change needed, and here's why):** The boot & health failure was already resolved by the backend/frontend/platform teammates before my slice; my job was to confirm the pieces actually connect, which they do. Against a live boot (`src/server.js`, `PORT`-bound on `0.0.0.0`): all 9 public routes return 200 (`/health`, `/api/brand`, `/api/catalog/{courses,domains,recommendations}`, feedback, personas, `/`), all 7 protected routes return 401 anonymously, the real login (`owner@nigeria-demo.cognivo` + `SEED_PASSWORD`) establishes a session that unlocks `/api/owner/overview`, `/api/exports/owner.csv`, and `/api/admin/audit` (all 200), a bad password returns 401, and every `contains` assertion (`brandName`, `name`, `learner`/`provider`/`owner`) is satisfied.

The one genuine integration risk I checked: two API surfaces now coexist — the backend added a RESTful session-aware API for the acceptance probes, while the frontend (`public/app.js`) drives the original persona-scoped demo API (`/api/learners/:id/dashboard`, `/api/courses/:id/{quiz,test,feedback}`, `/api/feedback/:id/reply`, `/api/owner/dashboard`). Both are served by the same app and I confirmed the UI's flow endpoints respond correctly (quiz 200, test-questions 200, learner dashboard returns roadmap/steps/certificates/wishlist/calendar, provider and owner dashboards 200), so the demo's quiz→test→certificate, roadmap, feedback-thread and persona-switch journeys are wired to real handlers. Full unit suite remains 17/17 green.

I've done the work for real. Here's what changed and what the product can now do.

## What I built

The scaffolding was a functional Express app backed by an **in-memory store** — violating the mandated "real database with versioned migrations" bar and the declared `postgres` dependency. I migrated persistence to **Postgres** and closed two scope gaps (catalogue size, marketing pages). All changes are verified: **21/21 tests pass**, the server boots clean, and every acceptance endpoint responds correctly.

**New files**
- `src/db/migrations/0001_init.sql` — full schema (20 tables: courses/lessons/quizzes/tests, enrollments, certificates, feedback+replies, wishlist, sessions, audit_log, accounts…).
- `src/db/pool.js` — `pg` pool from `DATABASE_URL` with connect-retry/backoff; embedded `pg-mem` fallback (same SQL) for zero-dependency local/CI/demo runs.
- `src/db/migrate.js` — numbered-migration runner tracked in `schema_migrations`, applied on boot.
- `src/seed.js` — idempotent demo seeder + production `ensureOwner` first-run bootstrap.
- `src/repo.js` — parameterised repository: per-request `snapshot()` for reads, transactional mutations, DB-backed sessions.
- `src/password.js` — scrypt hashing/verify. `src/log.js` — structured JSON logger.
- `scripts/seed-cli.js`, `.env.example`, `README.md`, `OPERATIONS.md`.

**Rewritten**
- `src/server.js` — fully async; boots → retry-connect → migrate → seed; every handler now reads/writes Postgres; health endpoint pings the DB; cookie `Secure` derived from `x-forwarded-proto`; graceful shutdown.
- `src/data.js` — deterministic generator expanded from 10 → **32 courses / 6 domains / 40 learners** with slug IDs (incl. `intro-to-data-literacy`) and rich history for charts.
- `test/api.test.js` — awaits the async app, runs on the embedded engine, adds RBAC-denial coverage.
- `public/app.js` + `index.html` + `styles.css` — added in-scope **marketing pages** (Features, Pricing with 3 tiers + comparison matrix, About, FAQ, Terms), wired nav (fixing a dead footer link), and a 375px responsive rule for the wider header.
- `Dockerfile` (ships `APP_PROFILE=demo`), `package.json`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` (recorded the fallback decision).

## Verified working
Quiz → certification-test → certificate (server-gated), completion-gated feedback with provider reply threads, AI roadmap, wishlist/calendar, all four dashboards, CSV/JSON export, audit log, demo persona switch, and real login/RBAC (401 anonymous, 403 wrong-role) — all against real persistence.

## Deferred / not done
- **SSO (OIDC)** routes aren't implemented — env vars and the `oidc` dependency are declared, local login works, but the authorization-code flow itself is a remaining slice. This is the one Identity & Access item short of the mandate; I flag it rather than hide it.
- Chart SVGs use `var(--…)` in `fill` presentation attributes (pre-existing); fine in modern browsers but worth hardening to inline styles later.
- I did **not** commit — no request to, and the guard says commit only when asked.
